title: Tech Note: Breaking the Rules to Improve Performance, Part 2—Using 4D's Built-In Relational Lookups
author: Walt Nelson
featured_technology: 4D built-in relational lookups (Automatic Relate one, wildcard support)

historical_commentary.text: This note argues for deliberately using 4D's built-in many-to-one relational lookup mechanism (and denormalized 'Wildcard_Choice' concatenation fields) instead of hand-written custom lookups, for speed reasons that mattered enormously over WAN or dial-up connections in the mid-1990s. The specific performance motivation (dial-up modem latency, WAN bandwidth constraints) is entirely obsolete given modern broadband and cloud connectivity, and the described built-in relational lookup UI and Customizer Plus-based Structure Font workaround reflect 4D's pre-V6, pre-ORDA procedural language era; the general principle of favoring built-in framework features over custom code for performance remains conceptually sound.
related_updates: Dial-up and WAN latency concerns central to this note's motivation are irrelevant on modern broadband/fiber and cloud-hosted deployments

4D's relational and data-access model has been substantially modernized with ORDA (Object Relational Data Access Model, introduced 2018), which supersedes this era's classic relation/lookup mechanisms for most new development
4D Customizer Plus, used here to set a monospaced Structure Font, is not part of the modern 4D toolset; font/UI settings are handled directly within current 4D preferences
